newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan body to announce Musashino bank rescue plan.
newsitem.headline: Japan body to announce Musashino bank rescue plan.

text.p: An association of Tokyo-based shinkin banks said on Thursday that it would announce a plan to bail out financially troubled Musashino Shinkin Bank.
A news conference will be held at 4 p.m. (0700 GMT), an association official said.
Shinkin banks are small credit associations which take deposits and lend mainly to members and are supervised by the Ministry of Finance (MOF).

Zenshinren Bank, a national association of credit associations, and Tokyo-based shinkin banks have been working out a programme to bail out Musashino Shinkin, which is reeling under problem loans now estimated at about 39 billion yen, industry sources said on Wednesday.

Under the programme now being worked out, Musashino's problem loans will be separated from healthy loans and those problem loans will be taken care of through financial aid provided by Zenshinren and other shinkin banks, they said. Musashino's business, including healthy loans and deposits, will be taken over by a shinkin bank, they added.
